about: The interior of the two ovaries: the fibrous capsule (tunica albuginea), the cortex and the medulla, the ovarian artery and vein entering at the hilum, the small follicles of the cortex, one dominant follicle with its oocyte (drawn in the right ovary), the corpus luteum that forms where it ovulated, and a corpus albicans scar (drawn in the left ovary). The dominant follicle and the corpus luteum follow the simulated menstrual cycle. The follicle's wall layers, the ligaments, the nerves and the true number and size of the small follicles are left out; the small follicles are drawn far larger than life so that they can be seen, and which ovary carries the dominant follicle is a drawing choice.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

parts.label: Tunica Albuginea
parts.summary: The dense fibrous capsule just under the surface of the ovary
parts.function: The tunica albuginea is a layer of dense connective tissue lying under the surface covering of the ovary. It gives the organ its firm, almond shape and encloses the cortex. It is drawn as a glass shell so that the follicles beneath it can be seen.

parts.label: Ovarian Cortex
parts.summary: The outer zone of the ovary, where the follicles lie
parts.function: The cortex is the outer part of the ovary and contains the follicles at every stage of development, together with the scars left by those that have ovulated. Follicle-stimulating hormone drives the growth of follicles within it. It is drawn as glass, and it becomes a little more vivid when follicle-stimulating hormone is high.

drives.note: Follicle-stimulating hormone acts on the follicles of the cortex.

parts.label: Ovarian Medulla
parts.summary: The central connective tissue core that carries the vessels
parts.function: The medulla is the central part of the ovary, made of loose connective tissue with many blood vessels and nerves, which reach it from the hilum. It is drawn as a glass core with the vessels running through it.

parts.label: Ovarian Artery
parts.summary: The artery that supplies the ovary, entering at the hilum
parts.function: The ovarian artery reaches the ovary through the ligaments that suspend it and enters at the hilum, then branches through the medulla towards the cortex. The blood streaming in is coloured by the simulated arterial oxygen saturation, and it runs faster when the corpus luteum is large, because that structure is richly supplied with blood.

drives.note: The corpus luteum is a highly vascular structure.

parts.label: Ovarian Vein
parts.summary: The vein that carries blood and hormones away from the ovary
parts.function: Blood leaves the medulla through veins that gather at the hilum and drain the organ. The blood carries away the hormones the ovary secretes. It is coloured by the simulated venous oxygen saturation.

drives.note: The venous drainage carries the ovarian hormones, estradiol among them, into the circulation.

parts.label: Primordial Follicles
parts.summary: The reserve of resting follicles, each an oocyte in a thin layer of cells
parts.function: Primordial follicles are the resting reserve, each a single immature egg cell surrounded by a flat layer of cells. They lie close under the capsule. In life they are far too small to see; here they are drawn as beads so that the cortex reads as a population.

parts.label: Growing Follicles
parts.summary: Primary and secondary follicles, enlarging in the cortex
parts.function: Some of the follicles in the cortex begin to enlarge, gaining layers of cells around the egg. Their later growth depends on follicle-stimulating hormone. They brighten when follicle-stimulating hormone rises.

drives.note: Follicle-stimulating hormone supports the growth of the developing follicles.

parts.label: Dominant Follicle
parts.summary: The one follicle that grows to ovulate; it makes estradiol as it grows
parts.function: In each cycle one follicle outgrows the rest and fills with fluid. As it grows it makes more estradiol, and in the middle of the cycle a surge of luteinising hormone causes it to rupture and release its egg. In this simulator its size follows the follicular growth of the cycle and it glows with estradiol. At ovulation it collapses and disappears, and it is hidden in the luteal phase and when the body is pregnant or not cycling.

drives.note: Its growth is the follicular growth of the cycle.
The growing follicle is the main source of estradiol before ovulation.

parts.label: Oocyte
parts.summary: The egg cell, held on the wall of the fluid-filled follicle
parts.function: The oocyte lies within a small mound of cells on the wall of the follicle. At ovulation it is released with some of the surrounding cells and carried towards the fimbriae of the uterine tube. It is shown here much larger than life.

drives.note: The luteinising hormone surge triggers its release.

parts.label: Corpus Luteum
parts.summary: The yellow body formed from the follicle after ovulation; it makes progesterone
parts.function: After ovulation the wall of the ruptured follicle becomes the corpus luteum, a yellow endocrine body that secretes progesterone and some estradiol. If pregnancy does not follow, it regresses; if it does, human chorionic gonadotropin keeps it active. In this simulator it grows and glows with its activity in the cycle and, when the body is pregnant, with the corpus luteum and hCG drives.

drives.note: Its size and secretion follow its place in the luteal phase.
Human chorionic gonadotropin maintains the corpus luteum in early pregnancy.

parts.label: Corpus Albicans
parts.summary: The pale scar left when a corpus luteum has regressed
parts.function: When a corpus luteum regresses it is replaced by a small white scar of fibrous tissue, the corpus albicans, which slowly shrinks in the cortex. It makes no hormones, so it does not glow. It is drawn in the opposite ovary to the dominant follicle.

parts.label: Suspensory Ligament of the Ovary
parts.summary: The fold of peritoneum that carries the ovarian vessels up to the ovary
parts.function: The suspensory ligament runs from the upper pole of the ovary up and out over the pelvic brim and carries the ovarian artery, vein and nerves. It is drawn as one cord on each side.

parts.label: Ovarian Ligament
parts.summary: A fibrous cord from the lower pole of the ovary to the uterus
parts.function: The ovarian ligament joins the ovary to the side of the uterus just below the tube, within the broad ligament. It keeps the ovary near the uterus.

parts.label: Mesovarium
parts.summary: The short fold of peritoneum that attaches the ovary to the back of the broad ligament
parts.function: The mesovarium is the fold through which the vessels reach the hilum of the ovary. The ovary is the only pelvic organ not covered by peritoneum. It is drawn as a thin sheet at the hilum border.

parts.label: Hilum of the Ovary
parts.summary: The border of the ovary where the vessels enter and leave
parts.function: The hilum is the slit-like attached border of the ovary. Through it the ovarian artery, vein and nerves pass in and out of the medulla.

parts.label: Surface Epithelium
parts.summary: The single layer of cells that covers the ovary
parts.function: The surface of the ovary is covered by a single layer of cuboidal cells, the germinal epithelium, which lies over the tunica albuginea. It is drawn as a thin glass skin.

parts.label: Primary Follicles
parts.summary: The first growing stage of a follicle
parts.function: A primary follicle has an enlarging oocyte surrounded by a layer of cuboidal granulosa cells. It is drawn as a few beads, enlarged to be seen.

parts.label: Secondary (Antral) Follicles
parts.summary: A growing follicle with several layers of granulosa cells and a fluid-filled space
parts.function: In a secondary follicle the granulosa cells have formed several layers, a theca has formed round them and pockets of fluid are merging into an antrum. Follicle-stimulating hormone drives this stage. It is drawn as a few larger beads.

parts.label: Antrum
parts.summary: The fluid-filled cavity of the mature follicle
parts.function: The antrum holds follicular fluid and enlarges as the follicle grows towards ovulation. It is drawn as a glass sphere at the centre of the follicle.

parts.label: Granulosa Cells
parts.summary: The cells that line the wall of the follicle
parts.function: The granulosa cells form the wall inside the follicle. They make oestrogen from androgens made by the theca, and after ovulation they form the granulosa-lutein cells of the corpus luteum. They are drawn as a glass shell.

parts.label: Theca Interna
parts.summary: The inner, vascular layer of the follicle wall
parts.function: The theca interna is a cellular, richly vascular layer round the granulosa. Under luteinising hormone it makes androgens, which the granulosa converts to oestrogen.

parts.label: Theca Externa
parts.summary: The outer, fibrous layer of the follicle wall
parts.function: The theca externa is a capsule of connective tissue round the follicle, which merges with the stroma of the ovary.

parts.label: Cumulus Oophorus
parts.summary: The mound of granulosa cells that carries the oocyte
parts.function: The cumulus oophorus is the heap of granulosa cells on the wall of the follicle in which the oocyte sits, projecting into the antrum. It goes with the oocyte at ovulation.

parts.label: Zona Pellucida
parts.summary: The clear glycoprotein coat round the oocyte
parts.function: The zona pellucida is a translucent layer between the oocyte and the cells around it. Sperm must bind to and pass through it at fertilisation. It is drawn as a glass shell.

parts.label: Corona Radiata
parts.summary: The ring of granulosa cells that stays attached to the oocyte
parts.function: The corona radiata is the innermost layer of the cumulus cells, which stays on the outside of the zona pellucida and goes with the oocyte at ovulation. It is drawn as a ring of beads.

parts.label: Granulosa-Lutein Cells
parts.summary: The large central cells of the corpus luteum, derived from the granulosa
parts.function: After ovulation the granulosa cells enlarge into granulosa-lutein cells, which make progesterone and oestrogen. They form most of the bulk of the corpus luteum. They are drawn as a glass core.

parts.label: Theca-Lutein Cells
parts.summary: The smaller cells at the edge of the corpus luteum, derived from the theca interna
parts.function: The theca-lutein cells lie in the folds round the granulosa-lutein cells and make progesterone and androgens. They are drawn as a ring of beads at the edge.
